why: the positive control: a declared key holding one value links its one subject and the receipt's figure projects onto it — a linker that links nothing must not pass this corpus by silence

the first adversarial class: the identifier's value repeated under an UNDECLARED key must produce exactly one link — a linker joining on value coincidence would link a note to a job it merely mentions

a declared PATH binds nothing when the value sits under the same NAME somewhere else: data.job_id is declared, the payload carries meta.job_id, and a flat name match here is the wrong-link mistake that manufactures contradictions

one declared key holding two different values across the receipt's blocks identifies nothing — which of them is the subject is a question the receipt does not answer — and the miss is COUNTED as ambiguous, never guessed at

a receipt naming TWO kinds of subject links both but writes NO identifier fact — the kernel projects every live triple of a linked entity onto every subject it is linked to, so an identifier fact here would put the job's id onto the asset and manufacture a contest two calls never had

the second adversarial class: one value under two declared kinds spells two DISTINCT subjects (job:X-77 and asset:X-77 share nothing but bytes), and the cross-kind guard REFUSES to write either identifier onto the shared receipt — so neither subject can ever inherit the other's identity off the coincidence

a receipt of nothing but handles of several kinds holds no fact for a link to be a claim about: linking would need the identifier facts the cross-kind guard forbids, so it links NOTHING and each identity is counted unlinked — the design's stated cost, pinned
the two-phase flow the design is built on: a submit that returns ONLY a handle of one kind writes the identifier fact and links, so the status call's figures later join the same subject

the v1 bound: a NUMBER under a declared key is a figure, not an identity — the harvest already asserts it, and spelling job:5 beside the figure 5 would be two facts nobody can tell apart later. Not ambiguity either: skipped without a count

a [] path with three elements links nothing and is counted: three list elements are three distinct subjects the receipt is legitimately about, v1 has no per-element entity to keep one link from carrying another's identity, and guessing one would be the wrong-link mistake
the same [] declaration at length one is unambiguous and binds: the pair with the probe above pins the boundary exactly at one, not at 'small'

a declared value carrying whitespace cannot round-trip as kind:value, so the kernel refuses the link and the runtime COUNTS the refusal — cognition must survive the receipt, because a crash here would cost a mission its whole shadow over one hostile payload
